teaser.text: Trane Technologies sells equipment and services that control temperature wherever heat matters. Its dollar comes from building, installing and maintaining those systems, then goes to materials, people, delivery and the overhead of running the business.

stock.title: Trane stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Trane’s stock forecast spans bear, base and bull cases, hinging on profitable backlog conversion, cash generation and valuation.
stock.opening: Trane’s weighted forecast is $503.29 in October 2027 and reaches $556.94 in October 2029. It hinges on whether Trane converts the $12.1B backlog profitably.
stock.closing: The full Trane memo also answers questions about its business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Trane’s shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast’s central outcome is a moderate gain, but the possible outcomes spread widely. The weighted price is $503.29 in October 2027 and $529.16 in October 2028. It reaches $556.94 in October 2029, representing returns with dividends of 12% and 19% at the first two dates, then 26%.
By October 2029, the bear case gives $301.00 while the bull case reaches $911.46, against today’s $451.29. The bear probability is 25%. The base probability is 55%. The bull probability is 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Trane?

paragraphs.text: The bear case gives $3,219M in the first year and $3,250M in the second. It reaches $3,302M in 2029 as revenue rises only from $24,200M to $25,800M while margins fall from 13.3% to 12.8%. The bull case reaches $5,389M by 2029, using revenue of $31,700M and a 17.0% margin. The difference reflects whether the $12.1B backlog converts profitably. Q2 bookings rose 37% organically, but gross margin fell to 35.6% from 37.6%, and price versus inflation was unfavorable. Guidance of $15.20–$15.30 adjusted EPS supports growth, but Stellar is expected to add $500M of revenue with no 2026 EPS contribution.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Trane really make?

paragraphs.text: Trane’s own free-cash-flow count reached $2,887.3 million because it added back selected restructuring, legal and acquisition payments and included an asset sale. A stricter analytical measure subtracts stock compensation, which represented $86.6 million in 2025. These are different definitions, not different piles of cash.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Trane today?

paragraphs.text: The trailing P/E compares the share price with recent earnings; the forward P/E uses estimated future earnings. Trane’s trailing P/E is 33.6×, while its forward P/E is 25.5×. Those multiples imply past earnings of about $13.43 per share and expected earnings of about $17.70. The lower multiple therefore assumes profits will rise. Adjusted earnings also exclude selected acquisition, restructuring and acquired-backlog amortization costs, so investors must check whether growth appears in organic sales and margins.

dividend.title: Trane dividend: payout, coverage and yield
dividend.meta_description: Trane dividend coverage, payout history, plans and yield against the share price.
dividend.opening: Trane pays a quarterly dividend of $1.05 per share, up from $0.94. In 2025, Trane generated $2,837.4 million of free cash flow, while dividends and buybacks used $2,318.6 million, leaving $492.1 million after payments to minority owners.
dividend.closing: The full memo explains Trane’s business, rivals, management, risks and what could shape its future.

blocks.heading: How much does Trane pay per share over the years shown?

paragraphs.text: The company continues to favor distributions. A $5.0 billion buyback authorization permits purchases over time but does not require immediate spending. The quarterly dividend rose from $0.94 to $1.05. Buybacks also reduced diluted weighted-average shares from 225.1 million to 222.5 million, giving each remaining share a larger claim on future earnings. Whether those repurchases created value depends on the prices paid.

blocks.heading: Does Trane’s cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: The balance improved later. Acquisition spending reached $862.8 million in 2023, while shareholder payments fell to 63.6% of free cash flow. In 2025, free cash flow reached $2,837.4 million. Dividends and buybacks absorbed $2,318.6 million, or 81.7%, leaving $492.1 million after payments to minority owners. Trane spent $276.0 million on acquisitions, yet cash still rose by $173.2 million.

paragraphs.text: For 2026, management guides to 11.5% reported revenue growth and 9.0% organic growth. It guides to adjusted continuing EPS of $15.20–$15.30. It expects 11.5% organic growth in the second half, including 10.0% in the quarter to September. It targets free cash flow equal to 100.0% of adjusted net earnings for 2026.

The dividend base path is $4.15, $4.55 and $4.95 per share. It assumes roughly 9% annual growth, below the recent 12%–14% record. The bear freezes the current $4.20 rate, while the bull reaches $5.35 through roughly 13% growth. The $900M 2026 dividend plan supports continued payment, but does not promise future DPS growth.

blocks.heading: What is Trane’s dividend yield against its share price?

paragraphs.text: The dividend yield is only 0.9%, so the stock offers little immediate income. Trane reported $2.9 billion of free cash flow in 2025, equal to 98% of adjusted net earnings. That cash coverage makes reinvestment and future growth more important to the investment case than current distributions.

earnings.title: Trane earnings: guidance and what to watch
earnings.meta_description: Trane's October 29, 2026 results will test guided growth, adjusted EPS and cash collection.
earnings.opening: Trane reports its next results on October 29, 2026. Watch whether sales arrive on schedule, profit holds on those sales and customer collections keep pace.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains Trane's business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

paragraphs.text: On July 30, Trane raised its full-year outlook to 11.5% reported revenue growth and 9.0% organic growth. Organic growth removes acquisitions and currency effects, so it asks whether businesses Trane already owned are selling more. Management expects continuing GAAP EPS, meaning earnings per share under standard accounting rules, of $15.00–$15.10. Its adjusted range, which excludes selected items to clarify operating performance, is $15.20–$15.30.

The calendar explains why the second-half target is higher. The full-year rate blends the first half with the remaining months, so slower earlier growth requires stronger performance later. Management expects third-quarter organic growth of 10.0% and adjusted EPS of $4.70. Those figures depend on completing orders and recognizing sales, not simply receiving new bookings.

blocks.heading: Did Trane keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Promises must be judged against the forecast originally made. In July 2025, management projected about 8% organic revenue growth and adjusted earnings of about US$13.05 per share. “Organic” means growth from the existing business, excluding acquisitions and currency effects. In October, management cut the growth forecast to about 6% and set adjusted earnings at US$12.95–13.05. Final results were 6% growth and US$13.06 per share. Earnings were essentially delivered, but the original sales ambition was not.

blocks.heading: What has Trane's revenue and profit done?

paragraphs.text: The tables show revenue rising while growth slows, operating margin rising as the latest real free cash flow margin turns, and net debt moving with cash generation and working capital. Trane’s computed free cash flow per share—cash from operations minus capital spending—and diluted EPS recovered from earlier years, while payouts exceeded free cash flow in the first two years shown. The diluted share count shrank as buybacks and stock-based pay shaped each share’s claim; valuation assumes earnings growth while adjusted earnings exclude selected costs.

blocks.heading: What should Trane watch in its next results?

paragraphs.text: Trane reports third-quarter results on October 29. The test is whether sales arrive on schedule, profit holds on those sales and customer collections keep pace. Management has guided to 10.0% organic growth and $4.70 adjusted EPS. The fourth-quarter outlook will show whether the acceleration is temporary or becoming the new run rate.
